newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Union in deal with Canadian miner.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Union in deal with Canadian miner.

text.p: Union Mining NL said on Wednesday it had signed a heads of agreement with Canadian mining company Arkaroola Mining Ltd with respect to funding further exploration on the company's exploration permits in north Queensland.
Union said Arkaroola will spend A$2 million over a period of three years starting on April 1, 1997 to earn a 50 percent interest in the tenements.

After Arkaroola has earned a 50 percent interest, Union has the right to either contribute or to elect to dilute to retain a minimum 25 percent interest through to a development decision being made, with all approvals to mine in place, it said.
The agreement is subject to due diligence by Arkaroola on the tenements to be completed by March 31, Union said.
Meanwhile, Arkaroola will reimburse Union the cost of the payment of the annual rentals of the mining leases at Croydon in north Queensland, which were paid on 31 December 1996, it said.

Union currently has reserves and resources of 740,000 tonnes at 3.6 grammes per tonne in the Croydon area contained in a number of mining leases, it said. Exploration will particularly target the potential that exists in the Croydon Area for a large low grade ore resource, the company said.
